answer: OpenSea trading volume history turns identity into something scarce. Because trades spread over a year, not a day, the terrace of a sybil is measured in real-world effort, not keystrokes. Honest agents barely notice the check, because trades spread over a year, not a day is something they already have; the spiral falls entirely on the farm, which must buy or steal it a hundred times. Clones stop being profitable the moment each one needs its own proof. The kernel is the margin: one proof is cheap, a hundred proofs are a business that loses money.
